variable-vs-individual.label: Confuses the individuals with the variables

numeric-label.label: Treats numeric labels as quantitative measurements

counts-vs-percents.label: Compares unequal groups using counts instead of percentages

majority-vs-plurality.label: Calls the largest category a majority without checking 50 percent

histogram-exact-values.label: Reads exact individual values from histogram bins

discrete-vs-continuous.label: Confuses discrete counts with continuous measurements

mean-resistant.label: Treats the mean as resistant to outliers

iqr-vs-range.label: Confuses the middle 50 percent with the full range

boxplot-whiskers.label: Extends boxplot whiskers through identified outliers

skew-mean-median.label: Reverses how skew pulls the mean relative to the median

zscore-percent.label: Interprets a z-score as a percentage

normal-tail.label: Uses the wrong tail of a normal distribution

conditional-denominator.label: Uses the overall total for a conditional percentage

conditioning-direction.label: Reverses which event is given in a conditional probability

association-from-totals.label: Infers association from unequal group totals

explanatory-response.label: Reverses the explanatory and response variables

correlation-causation.label: Treats correlation as proof of causation

correlation-linearity.label: Uses correlation without checking whether the pattern is linear

extrapolation.label: Trusts predictions beyond the observed explanatory values

residual-sign.label: Reverses actual minus predicted or its interpretation

residual-pattern.label: Treats a patterned residual plot as support for a linear model

least-squares.label: Minimizes raw residuals instead of squared residuals

rsquared-points.label: Interprets r-squared as the percent of points on the line

intercept-context.label: Assumes the intercept is meaningful when zero is outside the context

leverage-residual.label: Confuses a large residual with high leverage

sample-population.label: Confuses the observed sample with the target population

selection-bias.label: Treats an unrepresentative sample as representative

large-sample-bias.label: Assumes a large sample removes selection bias

observational-causation.label: Claims an observational study establishes cause and effect

stratified-cluster.label: Confuses sampling within every stratum with selecting whole clusters

nonresponse-voluntary.label: Confuses nonresponse with voluntary response bias

random-selection-assignment.label: Confuses random selection with random assignment

blocking-randomization.label: Forms blocks randomly instead of using a relevant characteristic

short-run-balance.label: Expects random outcomes to balance out in the short run

expected-guaranteed.label: Treats a long-run expected value as a guaranteed outcome

independent-disjoint.label: Treats independent events as mutually exclusive

addition-overlap.label: Adds event probabilities without subtracting their overlap

replacement-independence.label: Assumes repeated draws without replacement keep the same probabilities

binomial-geometric.label: Confuses a fixed number of trials with waiting for first success

sd-addition.label: Adds standard deviations instead of adding independent variances

sampling-individual.label: Confuses a sampling distribution with individual observations

sample-size-variability.label: Expects larger samples to make sample statistics more variable

unbiased-exact.label: Thinks an unbiased estimator gives the exact parameter every time

normality-conditions.label: Uses the wrong normality conditions for the statistic

confidence-probability.label: Assigns a confidence percentage as a probability to a fixed parameter in one interval

confidence-data.label: Interprets a confidence interval as containing a percentage of individual data

confidence-width.label: Expects higher confidence to produce a narrower interval

hypotheses-statistics.label: Writes hypotheses about sample statistics instead of population parameters

alternative-direction.label: Chooses a hypothesis direction that does not match the question

pvalue-null-probability.label: Interprets a p-value as the probability a hypothesis is true

pvalue-extreme.label: Counts only the exact observed outcome when interpreting a p-value

accept-null.label: Treats failure to reject as proof that the null hypothesis is true

pvalue-decision.label: Reverses the comparison of p-value and significance level

paired-independent.label: Treats paired observations as independent samples

chi-square-expected.label: Uses observed counts when expected counts are required

categorical-quantitative.label: Confuses categories with measured or counted quantities
